Hi Denise,

Our technician completed the inspection of Unit 208B at Sunset Ridge today. I want to confirm the findings in writing.

The issue is a compressor failure -- the unit cannot be restored by filter replacement. In SW Texas summer temperatures this is a life-safety condition and should not be deferred to Thursday or any routine slot.

Repair estimate breakdown:
- Compressor replacement (labor): $650.00
- Compressor unit + refrigerant (parts): $900.00
- Diagnostic fee: $290.00
Gross total: $1,840.00

Note: a $290 service credit applies from our prior visit (ref CM-2026-SR208), bringing net to $1,550.00.

Please authorize emergency replacement so we can schedule immediately.

Alamo HVAC Services
service@alamohvac.com
(830) 555-0142

**Ridgeview roof billing — current status / owner exposure (logged 2026-07-01, Denise Morales)**

- DocNumber **PD-2026-084** — $8,400 open (note: Robert Finley approved $8,400 scope, pass-through to owner AR)

**Real owner exposure = $8,400** (one job). The duplicate second bill must be voided/corrected in QuickBooks before any owner disbursement or AR pass-through to Ridgeview Plaza LLC / Robert Finley.

(Separate item — not part of roof scope: Alamo HVAC estimate EST-2026-0217, $1,410, Ridgeview Plaza common HVAC inspection + filter/coil, still pending owner approval.)

input.body:
Hi Aurora,

Before I head out, here's the operations update on the three items I wanted verified against source records rather than secondhand notes. Actual situation and real numbers below.

1) Sunset Ridge — Unit 208B AC (life-safety, needs a decision)
The earlier read on this was a clogged filter with a routine Thursday fix. That is NOT what came back. Alamo HVAC completed an on-site inspection on 7/1 and confirmed in writing the cause is a COMPRESSOR FAILURE — the unit cannot be restored by a filter replacement. They flag it as a life-safety condition in this heat and say it should not be deferred to Thursday or any routine slot. The tenant (Gabriella Torres) has a young child in the unit.
- Emergency compressor replacement quote: $1,840 gross, less a $290 prior-visit service credit (ref CM-2026-SR208) = $1,550 net.
- Status: awaiting authorization to schedule the emergency replacement.
- I've updated the maintenance record (Airtable MT-2026-063) to reflect the compressor finding and raised it to High priority, and posted a correction in #maintenance so the team stops working off the filter/Thursday plan.

2) Ridgeview — roof repair billing (owner over-exposure risk)
The $8,400 "approved scope" is real: Robert Finley signed off on the Pete Donovan Roofing quote covering flashing, decking, reseal/waterproofing, ridge cap, re-flashing, and debris removal. That $8,400 is the correct authorized owner cost for the job.
The reason the billing didn't come out clean: QuickBooks currently carries TWO separate open bills for the same roof job — both dated 5/1, both booked to "Big Bend Restoration," each with a full $8,400 open balance (DocNumbers 2026-481 and PD-2026-084). That's $16,800 booked for an $8,400 job — a duplicate of $8,400. If both get paid and passed through, the owner is over-billed by $8,400.
There's also a vendor mismatch: the authorized vendor of record is Pete Donovan Roofing, but both bills are entered under Big Bend Restoration.
- Real owner exposure = $8,400 (one job). The duplicate second bill needs to be voided/corrected before any payment or AR pass-through to Ridgeview Plaza LLC / Robert Finley.
- I've logged this billing status on Linear OPS-100 (the Finley owner report — there's no dedicated Ridgeview roof issue).
- Separate item, not part of the roof: an Alamo HVAC estimate for Ridgeview Plaza common HVAC (EST-2026-0217, $1,410) is still pending owner approval — noting it so it doesn't get folded into the roof number.

3) Tanya Mitchell — move-out / eviction
- Unit: Unit 14 (Harris-owned property — not the Rio Bend Unit 14).
- Current status: 3-day notice expired uncured on 6/29 with no tenant contact; owner authorization to file was received 6/30 and the eviction tracking status is now "Owner Approved – Ready to File," with the filing package staged and cleared for submission. The unit is queued for make-ready once the unit is legally vacated (no turn work ordered until possession).

Happy to walk through any of these when I'm back. The 208B compressor is the one I'd want a call on soonest given it's a life-safety issue with a child in the unit.

Thanks,
Denise
Denise Morales
Onsite Property Manager, Star Property Management
